<Note>
  For direct calls with `worker.trigger` or `iii trigger`, see [Using iii /
  Functions](./functions#triggering-invoking-functions). This page shows how to register (bind)
  triggers to functions, gate triggers with a condition, and unregister triggers.
</Note>

## Register a trigger

<Note>
  To author a worker, see [Creating Workers /
  Triggers](../creating-workers/triggers#bind-a-function-to-an-existing-trigger-type) for the
  difference between registering a trigger and registering a trigger type.
</Note>

Bind a trigger from a worker's trigger type (for example an `http` request, a `cron` schedule, or a
`state` change) to a function. For the trigger concept, see
[Understanding iii / Triggers](../understanding-iii/index#triggers). You can also
[write your own](../creating-workers/triggers).

You bind triggers to functions via the `function_id`. The trigger declares its `type`, its `config`
(defined by each type), and the function to invoke.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    import { registerWorker } from "iii-sdk";

    const url = process.env.III_URL;
    if (!url) throw new Error("III_URL must be set");
    const worker = registerWorker(url, { namespace: "orders" });

    worker.registerTrigger({
      type: "http",
      function_id: "math::add",
      config: { api_path: "/math/add", http_method: "POST" },
    });
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    import os
    from iii import register_worker, InitOptions

    worker = register_worker(
        os.environ.get("III_URL"),
        InitOptions(worker_name="my-worker", namespace="orders"),
    )

    worker.register_trigger({
        "type": "http",
        "function_id": "math::add",
        "config": {"api_path": "/math/add", "http_method": "POST"},
    })
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    use iii_sdk::protocol::RegisterTriggerInput;
    use iii_sdk::{InitOptions, register_worker};
    use serde_json::json;

    let url = std::env::var("III_URL").expect("III_URL must be set");
    let worker = register_worker(
        &url,
        InitOptions {
            namespace: Some("orders".into()),
            ..Default::default()
        },
    );

    worker.register_trigger(RegisterTriggerInput::new(
        "http",
        "math::add",
        json!({ "api_path": "/math/add", "http_method": "POST" }),
    ))?;
    ```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

Each worker's Worker Docs describe the config, payload, and result shape of its trigger types (for
example, [http](https://workers.iii.dev/workers/http) for the `http` type).

For example, the `http` worker sends the request to the function as the payload. The JSON request
body is in `payload.body`, next to `path_params`, `query_params`, and `headers`. The function
returns `status_code`, `headers`, and `body`, and the `http` worker sends them as the response.
Without `status_code`, the response status is `200`. Without `body`, the response body is `{}`.

### Trigger metadata

The optional `metadata` field on a trigger registration holds arbitrary JSON. In Node and Python,
add a `metadata` key next to `config`. In Rust, call `.with_metadata(json!({ ... }))` on
`RegisterTriggerInput`. The engine sends the metadata with the registration to the worker that
provides the trigger type. When the trigger fires, that worker sends the metadata to the target
function. The handler gets it as a second argument next to the payload. Support for metadata depends
on the trigger type. The `cron`, `state`, and `durable:subscriber` trigger types and the trigger
types of the `database` worker send it. The `http` trigger type does not send it. For other types,
check the Worker Docs for the trigger type.

When many triggers share one target function, the handler can use `metadata` to find which
registration fired. See
[Receive per-invocation metadata](../creating-workers/functions#receive-per-invocation-metadata) for
how a handler reads it in each SDK.

<Note>A direct `trigger()` call can also send `metadata`.</Note>

## Registering before a trigger type is available

Registration is order-independent. You can register a trigger before any worker provides its type.
For example, the worker that provides `http` has not connected yet. The engine stores the
registration and logs a pending notice. When a worker registers the trigger type in the namespace of
the worker that registered the trigger, or in `default`, the engine activates the stored
registration. A trigger that sets `trigger_namespace` uses only that namespace. See
[Trigger types and the two namespaces a trigger names](../understanding-iii/namespaces#trigger-types-and-the-two-namespaces-a-trigger-names).
When the providing worker restarts, the engine activates its stored registrations again.

Bind `math::add` to the `http` type, as shown in [Register a trigger](#register-a-trigger), before
the http worker runs. The engine accepts the registration and stores it. This walkthrough uses a
`math::add` that reads `payload.body` and returns its result in `body`.

Start the http worker afterward. The http worker calls the target function in its own namespace. Run
it in the namespace of `math::add` (`orders` in this example). This example uses a Compose daemon in
`orders`, so add `-n orders` to [`iii trigger`](../cli-reference/index#iii-trigger). The engine
activates the stored binding when the http worker provides `http` in the namespace of the worker
that registered the trigger, or in `default`. The http worker then sends requests on `/math/add` to
`math::add`, with no new registration.

```bash
# http worker started after registration
iii trigger -n orders compose::add worker=http

# the stored binding is now live on the http worker's default port (3111)
curl -X POST http://localhost:3111/math/add \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"a": 2, "b": 3}'
# the http worker sends the request to math::add through the activated trigger
```

For a known trigger type (for example `http`, `state`, `durable:subscriber`, or `stream`), the
pending notice shows the Compose command that adds the worker for that type. For other types, find
the worker that provides the type at [workers.iii.dev](https://workers.iii.dev).

A provider can reject the config of a registration (for example, a `cron` expression with five
fields). The SDK on the worker that sent the registration logs the error. What the engine does next
depends on the trigger type:

- For `http`, `cron`, `state`, and the trigger types of the workers that you write, the engine logs
  a warning and keeps the registration as `pending`. It tries the registration again when a worker
  registers the type again.
- For the `stream` trigger type, the engine logs an error and does not store the registration.
  Register the trigger again with a valid config.

For the error message format, see
[Engine protocol / `RegisterTrigger`](../reference/engine-protocol#registertrigger).

To list registrations with their `status` (`active` or `pending`), run
`iii trigger engine::registered-triggers::list include_pending=true`. Without `include_pending`, the
list shows only active registrations.

## Bind multiple triggers to one function

You can bind many triggers to one `function_id`, across any number of trigger types. Register a
second trigger with the same `function_id` and a different type or config. The same handler runs for
each trigger. Each trigger type sends its own payload shape, so the handler must accept each shape.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    // Same handler runs for an HTTP POST and a weekly cron tick.
    worker.registerTrigger({
      type: "http",
      function_id: "reports::generate",
      config: { api_path: "/reports/generate", http_method: "POST" },
    });

    worker.registerTrigger({
      type: "cron",
      function_id: "reports::generate",
      config: { expression: "0 0 9 * * Mon" }, // Every Monday at 09:00 UTC
    });
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    worker.register_trigger({
        "type": "http",
        "function_id": "reports::generate",
        "config": {"api_path": "/reports/generate", "http_method": "POST"},
    })

    worker.register_trigger({
        "type": "cron",
        "function_id": "reports::generate",
        "config": {"expression": "0 0 9 * * Mon"},  # Every Monday at 09:00 UTC
    })
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    use iii_sdk::protocol::RegisterTriggerInput;
    use serde_json::json;

    worker.register_trigger(RegisterTriggerInput::new(
        "http",
        "reports::generate",
        json!({ "api_path": "/reports/generate", "http_method": "POST" }),
    ))?;

    worker.register_trigger(RegisterTriggerInput::new(
        "cron",
        "reports::generate",
        json!({ "expression": "0 0 9 * * Mon" }), // Every Monday at 09:00 UTC
    ))?;
    ```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Gate a trigger with a condition

A trigger can carry an optional `condition_function_id` in its `config`. When the trigger fires, the
worker that provides the trigger type calls the condition function first, with the trigger payload.
The target `function_id` runs unless the condition returns `false`. If the condition function fails,
the target function does not run. The condition is a regular registered function. Support for this
field depends on the trigger type. Check the Worker Docs for the trigger type.

For the `http` type, the condition function gets the same request payload as the handler, without
the channel references `request_body` and `response`. When the condition returns `false`, the `http`
worker responds with status `422` and the error code `CONDITION_NOT_MET`. When the condition
function fails, it responds with status `500`. See [http](https://workers.iii.dev/workers/http).

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    worker.registerTrigger({
      type: "http",
      function_id: "orders::expedite",
      config: {
        api_path: "/orders/expedite",
        http_method: "POST",
        condition_function_id: "orders::is-priority",
      },
    });

    worker.registerFunction(
      "orders::is-priority",
      async (payload: { body: { customer_tier?: string } | null }) =>
        payload.body?.customer_tier === "gold",
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    worker.register_trigger({
        "type": "http",
        "function_id": "orders::expedite",
        "config": {
            "api_path": "/orders/expedite",
            "http_method": "POST",
            "condition_function_id": "orders::is-priority",
        },
    })

    def is_priority(payload: dict) -> bool:
        body = payload.get("body") or {}
        return body.get("customer_tier") == "gold"

    worker.register_function("orders::is-priority", is_priority)
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    use iii_sdk::RegisterFunction;
    use iii_sdk::protocol::RegisterTriggerInput;
    use schemars::JsonSchema;
    use serde::Deserialize;
    use serde_json::json;

    #[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
    struct Order { customer_tier: Option<String> }

    #[derive(Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
    struct HttpPayload { body: Option<Order> }

    worker.register_trigger(RegisterTriggerInput::new(
        "http",
        "orders::expedite",
        json!({
            "api_path": "/orders/expedite",
            "http_method": "POST",
            "condition_function_id": "orders::is-priority",
        }),
    ))?;

    worker.register_function(
        "orders::is-priority",
        RegisterFunction::new(|input: HttpPayload| {
            Ok(input.body.and_then(|o| o.customer_tier).as_deref() == Some("gold"))
        }),
    );
    ```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Unregister a trigger

Trigger registration returns a handle with an `unregister()` method. Call it to drop the trigger at
runtime; when the worker disconnects, all of its triggers are removed automatically.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Node / TypeScript">
    ```typescript
    const trigger = worker.registerTrigger({
      type: "http",
      function_id: "math::add",
      config: { api_path: "/math/add", http_method: "POST" },
    });

    trigger.unregister();
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Python">
    ```python
    trigger = worker.register_trigger({
        "type": "http",
        "function_id": "math::add",
        "config": {"api_path": "/math/add", "http_method": "POST"},
    })

    trigger.unregister()
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Rust">
    ```rust
    use iii_sdk::protocol::RegisterTriggerInput;
    use serde_json::json;

    let trigger = worker.register_trigger(RegisterTriggerInput::new(
        "http",
        "math::add",
        json!({ "api_path": "/math/add", "http_method": "POST" }),
    ))?;

    trigger.unregister();
    ```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>
